subject: Segmented egress acceptance & IP assertion for Private VPC connectors
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.inference.com>
To: Terry Liu <terry.liu@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Segmented egress acceptance & IP assertion for Private VPC connectors

Terry — thanks again for the sync earlier. Following up with the specifics we need to finalize for the private VPC deployment: IP allowlisting, firewall policy expectations, and the acceptance artifacts your auditors will want. Attached: a short deck with our proposed egress options (egress-ip-deck.pdf) and a checklist (proofing-checklist.csv).

Summary of asks from Redwood: 
- Confirmation on whether Acme requires a single static CIDR per private connector, or if a small pool (up to 3 /28s) per region is acceptable.
- Whether all outbound to Redwood control plane and model runtime endpoints will be allowed over 443, or if you need additional inspected ports.
- Your preference for SNAT/Proxy (customer-owned proxy vs. Redwood-managed outbound proxy) and whether TLS inspection is in use.

Our recommended approach (high-level):
- Provide three static /28 blocks per region (US-East, US-West) for SNAT so you can allowlist concrete IPs.
- All control-plane traffic over TLS (443) to control.us.redwood-inference.com and model endpoints on runtime-us.redwood-inference.com. We’ll publish canonical FQDNs + check-in IPs for failover.
- Support split-horizon DNS for private endpoints; we will accept upstream CNAMEs for private resolver chains.
- Audit/evidence pack to include: signed IP assignment affidavit, TLS cert thumbprints, and a short runbook showing a synthetic curl/healthcheck you can execute.

Acceptance criteria we will meet before handover:
1) Documented static egress list (CIDRs and expected rotation policy).
2) Runbook for on-prem firewall team with sample iptables and SNI/SAN cert thumbprint checks.
3) Attestation PDF for procurement (SOC2 adjacency note).

Can you confirm the firewall team’s minimum requirements and whether Acme needs single /26 vs multiple /28s? If you prefer a call I can loop Marcus (runtime networking) and Laura (security/compliance) for a quick 30-min alignment.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: egress-ip-deck.pdf (presentation), proofing-checklist.csv (csv)
From: Terry Liu <terry.liu@acmehealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: acme-networking@acmehealth.com
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 12:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Segmented egress acceptance & IP assertion for Private VPC connectors

Priya — thanks for the clear summary. A few points from our networking team: 

- For procurement/audit simplicity we prefer one contiguous block where possible. If that's not feasible, two small blocks are acceptable but we prefer not to have more than three.
- Minimum allowed size: /26. We will accept /28s only if they are aggregated under a documented SNAT gateway and accompanied by a stable DNS-to-IP mapping.
- Example ranges we can provision now for testing: 34.201.120.0/26 and 54.152.8.0/26 — these are placeholder ranges; procurement will ask for the vendor-side IPs you will be NAT-ing to.
- TLS inspection: our security team performs TLS inspection on some appliances. If Redwood expects end-to-end mTLS, we need to know how that will interact with our intercepting proxies.

We will need your attestation for the static IPs and a simple failover matrix before our firewall team can sign off. Ops: ops@acmehealth.com — please coordinate next steps.

Regards,
Terry Liu
Head of Infrastructure, Acme Health

Terry / Priya — quick technical notes from the runtime team on implementation and acceptance tests.

Implementation approach we recommend:
- Redwood-managed egress gateway (preferred): Redwood deploys an outbound gateway per region that SNATs tenant traffic to a small pool of stable public IPs. That gives Acme a fixed allowlist and reduces complexity for rotation.
- Customer-managed proxy: If Acme needs to operate the SNAT, we can support upstream proxies — but we will require a documented mapping and periodic validation checks.

Concrete endpoints and ports we will use for acceptance tests:
- control.us.redwood-inference.com : 443 (TLS) — control plane (API key / mutual auth for management hooks)
- runtime-us.redwood-inference.com : 443 (TLS) — model runtime traffic
- health-checks (optional): https://runtime-us.redwood-inference.com/healthz (443)

Acceptance test (ops can run):
1) From your jumpbox, curl -vk https://runtime-us.redwood-inference.com/healthz and capture the outbound public IP (curl ifconfig.me).
2) Confirm that the observed public IP matches one of the CIDRs Redwood published in the signed IP assignment affidavit.
3) Perform a second check after a simulated failover (we will perform a controlled gateway restart) to confirm failover IPs match the expected failover list.

On TLS inspection: if Acme performs MITM TLS inspection, the connection from your proxy to our runtime will appear as a new TLS session — if you require end-to-end client certificate verification (mTLS) between your connector and Redwood, you will need to add Redwood’s CA as trusted on your proxy or disable interception for those flows. We can publish cert thumbprints for verification.

I attached a draft runbook (egress-proofing-runbook.md) with sample curl commands and iptables snippets. Happy to demo the checks during a call.

- Marcus
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Marcus — that runbook looks good. A couple follow-ups from our side: 

1) Split-horizon DNS: our on-prem resolver will return private internal IPs for runtime-us.redwood-inference.com. We need guidance on cache TTLs and whether Redwood will publish two different cert chains (private vs public).
2) TLS interception: our proxy team can add Redwood CA to the proxy, but we need the cert thumbprints and a short window where interception is disabled during the initial smoke tests.
3) Procurement: we need the exact static NAT IPs and a signed attestation by Redwood for each published block. The attestation should include expected rotation frequency and the fallback IPs.

Attached a short screenshot annotated by our firewall team showing how they expect to enter the rules (acme-screenshot-annotated.png).

Terry

1) We will provision and publish three static /28s per region for your sandbox (US-East). For production we can discuss aggregated /26s if procurement requires them.
2) We will produce a signed IP assignment affidavit and a short attestation doc (expected rotation: 90 days, emergency rotation documented with 24-hour notice and fallbacks).
3) Marcus will schedule a 30-min smoke test on Thu Oct 22 where we will: run the curl healthz check, capture outbound IP, and validate certificate thumbprints. Please confirm a time window when TLS interception can be suspended (ops@acmehealth.com).
4) Deliverables by Oct 22 EOD: signed affidavit PDF, runbook (finalized), and a small acceptance checklist you can hand to your firewall team.

If that timeline works, we’ll create the HubSpot milestone and shared Confluence page (links above). Please reply with a preferred time for the smoke test and confirmation on whether you require production /26s instead of our proposed /28s.

Thanks — Priya
